statements.t: “Our recent IPO positions Electra to build on our first-mover advantage in SIRP-targeted precision immune cell depletion,” said Kathy Dong, PharmD, MBA, President and Chief Executive Officer of Electra Therapeutics.

“Our deep expertise in SIRP biology and proprietary library of SIRP-targeting antibodies enable us to selectively address distinct pathogenic immune cell populations, creating therapeutic optionality across immune-mediated diseases and cancer.

We anticipate several important milestones in 2027, including ELA822 healthy volunteer data expected in the first half of the year, followed by ipsoprubart data in T/NK cell malignancies and completion of enrollment in the sHLH registrational program in the second half.”

The company’s global registrational program comprises SURPASS, a Phase 2/3 trial in newly diagnosed, treatment-naïve sHLH patients, and COMPASS, a retrospective natural history study designed to provide an external control comparator, with enrollment completion expected in the second half of 2027.
Based on this anti-tumor activity, the company is conducting an ongoing Phase 1 trial in patients with relapsed/refractory T/NK malignancies, with initial data expected in the second half of 2027.
The company plans to initiate a first-in-disease trial in patients with T cell-mediated immune disorders in mid-2027, subject to regulatory approval.

The company’s novel approach targets signal regulatory proteins (SIRP), a family of cell surface receptors whose expression is restricted to specific immune cell populations and increases upon activation, to enable selective depletion of disease-driving cells while preserving normal immune function.
